transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CSM) -- Evan Brooks (Procurement), Dana Li (Legal), Priyanka Rao (Infosec), Marcus Flynn (Platform Eng)

Summary:
Quick procurement/legal gating workshop to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations for a pilot, pricing approval path (procurement), and technical pilot scope for LLM inference (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Action items and next steps agreed at the end.

Topics:
- MSA and DPA redlines and non-starters
- SLA targets, error budgets, and rollback policies
- Pricing buckets: hosted per-token vs reserved/dedicated commits
- Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) connectivity, KMS/HSM, audit logs
- Pilot scope and success criteria, benchmark plan

Action items (summary): see metadata section above

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): okay hi everyone thanks for joining, uh we know procurement and legal are on, so we'll try to be crisp. Quick intros?
[00:00:12] Evan (Procurement): Evan here, procurement lead for Nimbus Health. We're focused on contract pathing and cost acceptance.
[00:00:18] Dana (Legal): Dana from legal, I'll be reviewing the MSA/DPA redlines and any data residency stuff.
[00:00:22] Priyanka (Infosec): Priyanka, infosec. We'll be validating KMS, audit logging, SOC2 proofs, that sort of thing.
[00:00:29] Maya: great, from Redwood we've got Luis, our solutions eng, and Priya CSM who will manage onboarding. Luis, want to kick to the pilot and SLA stuff?
[00:00:34] Luis (Redwood SE): Yeah thanks Maya. So high level, Redwood offers hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC or on-prem). For a pilot most folks start hosted for speed, then we can evaluate dedicated if you need predictable throughput. For Nimbus specifically you mentioned wanting private keys — can you confirm KMS needs?
[00:00:54] Priyanka: Yeah we need customer-managed keys; encryption at rest with our KMS and ideally HSM-backed keys. Also we need audit logs to show model access per token and per user.
[00:01:05] Luis: That's supported — Redwood Private supports customer KMS integration and we can ship audit logs. Note, in hosted we can do bring-your-own-key in certain tiers but dedicated/private gives the clearest guarantee.
[00:01:16] Marcus (Platform Eng): question on networking, if we do VPC peering what's the latency hit, and egress charging? We need to know egress fees up front.
[00:01:26] Maya: good call. Egress fees are in the pricing appendix; we can provide estimates based on token volume. For VPC we usually do private peering and there's no public egress, but there may be cross-region costs depending on topology. We'll include a template cost calc.
[00:01:38] Dana: on the MSA, our legal team has two non-starters: first, we cannot allow vendor data access clauses that imply logging of PHI in vendor systems without explicit handling; second, limitations on audits — we need to preserve right to audit or at least get SOC2 Type II report and a right-to-audit substitute.
[00:01:56] Maya: totally understood. We can provide SOC2 Type II and our security pack; for audit we generally provide attestation and can agree to an on-site or remote audit under narrow scope, or a summary report. We'll send the security pack link after the call.
[00:02:10] Priyanka: also need to confirm retention windows, specifically what temp KV caches or prefix caches are retained and for how long. That impacts PHI concerns.
[00:02:19] Luis: by default we use ephemeral KV cache for inference and we can disable persistent logging of inputs; but for debugging/monitoring customers sometimes opt-in to retention. We'll make sure the pilot runs with no retention and full redaction.
[00:02:29] Evan: good. Pricing — procurement wants a clear approval path. For pilot we're fine with hosted using credits, but if we go to production we need committed monthly pricing versus on-demand per-token.
[00:02:40] Maya: that's typical. We'll lay out two pathways: hosted (pay as you go) for pilot; dedicated reserved pool for production with commit tiers and discounted RU (request unit) pricing. We'll include sample math in the pricing appendix.
[00:02:51] Dana: quick on indemnity and data processing — can you confirm DPA supports EU Standard Contractual Clauses if needed? We have some cross-border data.
[00:03:02] Maya: yes DPA supports SCCs; we can append standard language. For Nimbus specifically we can map data residency controls.
[00:03:08] Priyanka: also need to know if KMS keys are exported or can stay in customer-controlled HSMs; service should never be able to export private key material.
[00:03:17] Luis: customer's key material never leaves their KMS/HSM; Redwood integrates with customer-managed KMS and we support key-wrap where applicable. There was a transcribe hiccup in my notes: we say 'K V cash' sometimes in the transcript but it's K V cache. Sorry.
[00:03:28] (laughter)
[00:03:30] Marcus: sounds good. On SLA numbers, procurement asked for 99.9% availability with defined error budget and credits. Is that something Redwood provides?
[00:03:39] Maya: we have SLA tiers. Hosted customers typically get 99.5; Dedicated can reach 99.9 with commit; Private deployments can have SLA in contract depending on ops mode. We'll propose 99.9 for dedicated with specifics on downtime credit and a rollback/fallback policy to a cheaper model if performance degrades.
[00:03:56] Dana: we need explicit incident notification timelines, root cause within 72 hours and a mitigation plan.
[00:04:03] Luis: we can commit to initial incident acknowledgement within 15 minutes for P1 and a root cause estimate within 72 hours — we'll capture exact wording in the SLA clause.
[00:04:13] Evan: procurement also flagged spike support — if we have bursts above reserved capacity, what's the burst policy and charges?
[00:04:20] Maya: for Dedicated you can enable burst capacity; it's metered with a burst rate and fallback model; we'll model charges as marginal price above baseline commit. For pilot, hosted auto-scales but charges are per token; we'll show both scenarios.
[00:04:33] Priyanka: one more infosec ask: pen test evidence and vulnerability disclosure timeline. We need yearly pen test and 30-day remediation windows for critical CVEs.
[00:04:43] Luis: Redwood publishes a yearly pen test summary and we have standard CVE SLAs; we'll make that explicit.
[00:04:49] (short pause)
[00:04:55] Dana: back to DPA redlines — we will send annotated DPA with three clauses: jurisdiction carveouts, data deletion and verification, and subprocessor list with 30-day notice before changes.
[00:05:07] Maya: understood. We usually publish subprocessors and notify customers of changes; we can accept 30-day notice in contract. On data deletion verification we can offer logs or deletion attestations.
[00:05:15] Evan: procurement timeline — if legal signs off quickly, we want procurement approval within two weeks. Is that feasible?
[00:05:22] Dana: two weeks is aggressive but possible if we don't have major redlines.
[00:05:26] Maya: we'll aim to get the redline to you within five business days post-call.
[00:05:31] Priyanka: technical pilot: Marcus, what do you need from us to run the bench?
[00:05:36] Marcus: runbook, sample payloads, expected QPS and P95 latency targets. Also how auth will flow — SSO or API keys and whether keys are rotated automatically.
[00:05:47] Luis: for auth we support SAML/SAML2 and OIDC for SSO, and API keys for service-to-service. For private connect we do mTLS with certificate-based auth. Key rotation is supported.
[00:05:57] Marcus: good. Regarding SAML, our IDP team will want a short window for setup.
[00:06:00] Maya: we'll include SSO setup notes in the onboarding doc.
[00:06:04] (background noise, brief overlap)
[00:06:10] Evan: procurement question on price floors — do you require a minimum committed spend for Dedicated?
[00:06:16] Maya: yes Dedicated has minimum commitment tiers; we'll propose a starter tier aligned to your expected baseline. For customers moving from hosted to dedicated we often do a credits conversion.
[00:06:26] Dana: anything around escrow for model weights or code? We have some regulatory requirements for business continuity.
[00:06:33] Luis: Redwood can include limited escrow provisions for specific enterprise customers; we can add an escrow schedule as an exhibit. We'll caveat that weight licensing is subject to model IP terms.
[00:06:44] Priyanka: network security — do you support private connectors and static egress IPs so we can whitelist?
[00:06:51] Luis: yes static egress IPs are available for Dedicated and Private; we'll supply the list pre-onboarding.
[00:06:57] Maya: quick note — some of the transcripts from other calls accidentally show 'Red wood Dedicate' or 'Redwood Infference' — ignore those, it's just transcription.
[00:07:05] (chuckle)
[00:07:08] Dana: liability caps — our legal wants to confirm liability caps align with our enterprise policy. Is there flexibility?
[00:07:15] Maya: standard commercial flexibility exists for enterprise deals; we can discuss liability caps in redlines.
[00:07:19] Evan: procurement will also need a stop-gain clause if latency breaches persist — basically a right to pause traffic and fallback to alternative provider or cached responses.
[00:07:29] Luis: we can include operational fallback playbooks and a canary rollback path; the SLA will specify failure thresholds that trigger fallback.
[00:07:36] Marcus: curious about observability — will we get per-route telemetry and token-level cost attribution? We want per-team cost reporting.
[00:07:44] Priya (CSM): Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards and tracing hooks. We can add your team email into the console and set up RBAC.
[00:07:56] Marcus: RBAC is critical — we need team-level permissions and least privilege for keys.
[00:08:01] Luis: RBAC, SSO groups and scoped API tokens are supported.
[00:08:04] (pause)
[00:08:12] Dana: one operational ask: if we take Dedicated, who manages patching and OS-level updates on the instances?
[00:08:20] Maya: for Hosted and Dedicated Redwood manages the runtime and underlying infra; for Private on-prem the customer owns infra patching but we provide ops playbooks. We'll write that into the ops responsibilities exhibit.
[00:08:31] Evan: procurement also asked about termination clauses and data return timelines post-termination. We need 30 days for data export and final deletion after confirmation.
[00:08:40] Maya: we can commit to exporting customer data within 30 days and final deletion attested after a further 7 days, subject to a few compliance checks. We'll put that in the DPA.
[00:08:50] Priyanka: please note any subject to legal hold exceptions.
[00:08:53] Dana: yes we'll flag that internally.
[00:08:57] (short silence)
[00:09:05] Luis: on performance, for the pilot we'll propose a small set of benchmarks: 1) p95 latency for a 512-token context at target QPS, 2) memory footprint and KV cache behavior, 3) concurrency scaling test. I'll attach the script and sample payloads.
[00:09:22] Marcus: can you run weight quantization tests? We are curious about quantized variants to reduce cost.
[00:09:27] Luis: yes we recommend quantized builds for Dedicated/Private; Redwood Optimize will give recommendations per workload. We'll show cost delta.
[00:09:34] Evan: procurement note — we need a single place for acceptance sign-off; who signs for Redwood side?
[00:09:40] Maya: I'll be the commercial owner and Luis will validate technical acceptance. We can draft an acceptance checklist for the pilot.
[00:09:46] Dana: legal needs to see the acceptance criteria in the MSA as an exhibit.
[00:09:50] Maya: sure, we'll include an exhibit with pass/fail criteria, test harness, and sample traffic.
[00:09:56] (background typing)
[00:10:05] Evan: curious about cross-region failover — if region X goes down, do you support routing to a backup region with data residency controls?
[00:10:14] Luis: yes routing policies support region fallback; for data residency we can configure routing policies that limit which models/regions can serve particular datasets. That will be in routing policy exhibit.
[00:10:25] Priyanka: regarding subprocessors — we need a list now and monthly updates.
[00:10:30] Maya: we publish subprocessors and can push a monthly change log.
[00:10:34] (slight overlap)
[00:10:40] Dana: about escrow again — is escrow standard or only on specific enterprise requests?
[00:10:45] Luis: it's an enterprise add-on, usually negotiated.
[00:10:48] Evan: procurement asks: if we exceed commit we want a blended overage rate cap to avoid runaway bills.
[00:10:56] Maya: we can propose a capped overage rate for a defined period while you scale; we'll include escalation paths.
[00:11:04] (brief pause)
[00:11:12] Priyanka: one small ask: telemetry retention — how long are audit logs retained and can we request a custom retention policy?
[00:11:19] Luis: default retention is 90 days but enterprise retention can be extended as a paid option; we can document retention windows and export endpoints.
[00:11:27] Dana: legal wants clause on subprocessor notification 30 days in advance; you confirmed earlier?
[00:11:32] Maya: yes we'll accept 30-day notice.
[00:11:36] Evan: on billing, do you support consolidated invoicing and PO terms?
[00:11:40] Maya: yes consolidated billing and net-30 invoicing are standard for enterprise. We can support PO numbers on invoices.
[00:11:47] Marcus: operations — will we get a staging environment mirroring production to run integration tests?
[00:11:52] Luis: yes we can provision a staging environment for the pilot. It will be functional parity but with lower performance SLAs.
[00:11:59] (sound of chair)
[00:12:04] Dana: any standard exclusions in your insurance that we should be aware of?
[00:12:09] Maya: we'll share our insurance binder; typically we carry cyber liability with specified caps. We'll send details post-call.
[00:12:15] Evan: timeline recap — if MSA/DPA get redlined and returned this week, procurement can route and approve next week, then pilot in two weeks.
[00:12:23] Maya: sounds good. Let's try to schedule bench run week of March 15th.
[00:12:29] (pause)
[00:12:35] Luis: technical note — if you plan to use long contexts, kernel selection and memory pinning matter; we'll advise on sequence length distribution for model selection. I'll surface recommended models.
[00:12:48] Marcus: what's the recommended quantization and expected perf win?
[00:12:52] Luis: quantization to 4-bit often gives 1.8-2.5x throughput improvement with some quality delta; we'll include model-specific numbers.
[00:12:59] Priyanka: any regulatory compliance beyond SOC2 — PCI or HIPAA? We handle PHI so HIPAA applicability is big.
[00:13:07] Dana: we need a HIPAA BA (business associate) addendum.
[00:13:11] Maya: Redwood can sign a BAA under our Private or Dedicated offerings; we'll flag legal to prepare a BAA template.
[00:13:19] Evan: procurement wants an exhibit for cost transparency — can you provide token-level cost examples and sample invoice?
[00:13:25] Maya: yes we'll share sample invoice and cost breakdown.
[00:13:29] (brief overlap, someone coughs)
[00:13:34] Luis: last technical note — for caching we do prefix/KV caching; if you want strict no-cache policy we can disable caching for the pilot.
[00:13:42] Priyanka: please disable caching for PHI-sensitive flows.
[00:13:45] Luis: noted.
[00:13:47] Dana: law ask — limitation-of-liability carveouts for willful misconduct?
[00:13:52] Maya: we can discuss carveouts, standard exceptions for gross negligence/willful misconduct typically remain.
[00:13:58] Evan: procurement follow-up — will you provide a signed SOW for pilot with acceptance criteria?
[00:14:04] Maya: yes pilot SOW + acceptance checklist. We'll share template.
[00:14:08] (small pause)
[00:14:15] Priyanka (CSM): I'll open the onboarding ticket and add Marcus and Evan, attach the security pack and initial SSO guide.
[00:14:23] Marcus: thanks. One more thing — can we get a 30-day rollback Q/A where we can opt out if performance impacts production?
[00:14:31] Maya: we can add a 30-day pilot review clause.
[00:14:34] Dana: good. Ok I'll send DPA redlines by Friday.
[00:14:38] Evan: procurement will aim for approval by March 20th if legal aligns.
[00:14:43] Maya: excellent. Quick recap of next steps: Maya send redlined MSA/DPA + SLA table; Luis send pilot scripts/runbook; Priya open onboarding ticket and send security pack; Marcus share network topology; Dana send DPA redlines.
[00:14:58] (closing remarks)
[00:15:02] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
[00:15:06] (call ends)

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-transcriptions: "K V cash" for KV cache, "Red wood Dedicate" for Redwood Dedicated, "sock two" for SOC2 in auto transcript. Links referenced: security pack (link shared in follow-up), SLA profiles and pricing appendix (will be shared by Maya).

End of transcript.
